text:
Detroit's lead was built in a 12-minute stretch that began just after Ottawa's, and the two teams' chances matched the scoreboard better than a 5-3 final suggests. Tim Stützle gave the Senators a 1-0 lead at 2:44 of the first, and Alex DeBrincat answered 32 seconds later. Dylan Larkin made it 2-1 at 13:14, and the Red Wings never trailed again. They out-chanced Ottawa 1.33 to 0.45 in expected goals in that period alone.

The game was effectively settled early in the second. Viktor Arvidsson scored on the power play at 2:01, a 33 percent chance, and Justin Faulk added a 12 percent look at 4:30 to make it 4-1. Drake Batherson cut it to 4-2 on a power play at 6:08, but Detroit's expected goals for the period (1.52 to 0.98) kept the lead comfortable. Detroit's 64 percent deserved-to-win figure fits: 3.56 expected goals to 2.62 overall, and 63 shot attempts to 52.

Ottawa did push back late. The Senators out-chanced Detroit 1.19 to 0.71 in the third, and William Eklund made it 4-3 at 10:30. DeBrincat sealed it with a power-play goal at 19:10, a chance worth only 8 percent, for his second of the night. Larkin, DeBrincat and Arvidsson took the three stars. Samuel Ersson allowed four goals against 3.47 expected, while John Gibson allowed three against 2.62.
